text: Investigating the `dayjs.tz()` Date/timestamp/Day.js-object parsing bug now (root cause is in the timezone plugin's input handling). ETA ~10 min.
Investigating the fractional-second timezone offset bug (`+08:59` instead of `+09:00`) now. ETA ~10 min.
Investigating the missing Dutch ordinal suffix in `format('Do')` for the `nl` locale now. ETA ~10 min.
Investigating the en-gb weekYear bug now (weekYear/weekOfYear plugins vs the locale's yearStart). ETA ~12 min.
Investigating the customParseFormat + zh-cn `A` token round-trip bug now. ETA ~12 min.
Investigating the `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms')` bug now. ETA ~12 min.

Fixed. `dayjs.tz()` now treats a Date, numeric timestamp, Day.js instance, or an offset/Z-bearing string as an instant (converted to the target zone's wall clock), while offset-less strings keep the existing wall-clock interpretation. `dayjs.tz(new Date('2020-08-07T12:00-07:00'), 'America/Vancouver').format()` is now `2020-08-07T12:00:00-07:00`, same for the timestamp and Day.js variants. Full test suite still green.

Fixed. The offset was computed from a millisecond-precision difference against a second-precision `toLocaleString`, leaving a fractional-minute offset. It is now rounded to whole minutes: `dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z')` gives `+09:00`. Full test suite still green.

Fixed. The `nl` locale's `ordinal` was a stub returning just `n.`. It now picks the Dutch suffix (`ste` for 1, 8 and 20+, `de` otherwise) and wraps the result in brackets so the `s`/`d` in the suffix aren't re-parsed as format tokens: 1ste, 2de, 8ste, 19de, 20ste. Full test suite still green.

Fixed. The duration plugin's unit table had no `milliseconds` entry, so `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms')` multiplied by `undefined` and produced an empty duration. Added the missing entry: `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').toISOString()` is now `PT0.001S`. Full test suite still green.

Fixed. `weekYear` only handled the forward rollover (December date in week 1 → next year) and never the backward one, so early-January dates belonging to the previous week-year were reported as the calendar year. It now returns `year - 1` when a January date falls in week 52/53. `dayjs('2021-01-01').locale('en-gb').weekYear()` is now 2020, 01-04 is 2021. Full test suite still green.
